objects.reconstructed: A finite-dimensional real inner-product space E with its Borel measurable structure; its concretely defined standard Gaussian gamma_E; an arbitrary scalar function f:E->R; one fixed arbitrary vector v:E; the Frechet derivative Df(x):E->L_R R.

domains.original: All E, including dimension zero, and every direction v including zero; no sphere or unit restriction.

quantifiers.original: For every carrier, f and chosen v, differentiability and the three integrability conditions precede one integral equality. Directional integrability concerns this v only.

All integrability hypotheses are specialized to the already chosen f and v.

assumptions.original: Exactly everywhere real Frechet differentiability and L1 Gaussian integrability of f, inner(x,v)*f, and Df(x)[v]. No C1, global derivative-norm, Lipschitz, support or decay premise.

No continuous derivative, C^1 regularity, compact support, boundary decay, nonzero v, unit v or whole-derivative-norm integrability is assumed.

conclusion.original: The finite Gaussian integral of inner(x,v)*f equals that of Df(x)[v]; no claim to derive the three assumed integrabilities.
conclusion.reconstructed: Integral over E of <x,v>f(x) against gamma_E equals integral over E of Df(x)[v] against gamma_E. Integrability is assumed, not asserted as a new conclusion.

scopes.original: Same actual standard Gaussian on both sides; ordinary real integrals over the entire carrier. No quotient, time or limiting identity.
